layout_summary: A two-column poster. A Sri Lankan mother leans in from the left edge with her face visible. One palm is raised high in a firm 'no', and her other hand comes down to push a dessert fork into a cake that already has a slice missing. The cake sits in an open, blank purple Kapruka cake box in the lower left. The right column holds a stacked, film-title-style serif headline at mid-height. One centred line of rounded bold purple copy runs across the bottom as the sign-off.

scene.subject: A Sri Lankan mother in her late 50s, wearing a simple cotton house dress, leans in from the left edge. Her shoulder and back are cropped by the edge, and her face is in three-quarter profile turned right. One hand is raised palm-out in a firm 'no, no, why did you spend money' gesture as she frowns at someone off-frame to the right. Her other hand pushes a dessert fork into an open chocolate cake that is already missing one slice. A small smudge of icing sits at the corner of her lips. The cake sits in a plain, blank, matte-purple cake box with its lid pushed back. Nothing else is in frame.
scene.composition: The figure runs diagonally from the lower-left edge (x=0, y≈52%) up to her raised palm at x≈24–36%, y≈10–28%. Her face is at x≈4–21%, y≈15–33%. Her other forearm drops vertically along x≈24% from y≈34% to y≈48%, where her hand and the fork span x≈21.5–28%, y≈48–55%. The cake box sits at x≈14.5–35%, y≈56–82.5% with its centre on the forearm axis, and its flat front face (x 15.5–31%, y 65–74.5%) is left blank for the logo. The figure is cropped at the left edge; the cake and box are complete.
scene.camera: Straight-on side view at about cake-box height for the box, and a near-profile three-quarter view of the mother. Long-lens feel with little perspective distortion, and everything sharp.
scene.lighting: Soft daylight key from the upper left with natural highlights on the chocolate glaze and skin, plus a faint soft contact shadow under the box. Clean neutral cream ground.
scene.prompt: Photographic cutout poster, 4:5 portrait, on a flat seamless warm-cream ground (#F5F4EB) with no room, no horizon and no backdrop texture. A Sri Lankan mother in her late fifties, in a simple muted-marigold cotton house dress, leans in from the left edge. Her shoulder and back are cropped by the frame, and her face is visible in three-quarter profile turned right, at about 4–21% across and 15–33% down. Mid-protest, she raises one palm high in a firm 'no' (fingertips near 36% across, 10% down) and frowns at someone off-frame to the right. Caught out, her other forearm drops straight down at about 24% across and pushes a dessert fork into a real chocolate cake. One slice is clearly gone, and a little icing is smudged at the corner of her lips. The cake sits in an open cake box, lid pushed back, at 14–35% across and 56–82% down. The box is matte purple #4B2386 and completely unprinted, with its flat front face fully visible. Soft daylight comes from the upper left, with one consistent light direction, a real soft contact shadow under the box, true skin texture and real fabric weave, and no plastic sheen. Straight-on long-lens view, everything sharp. Keep these areas empty, flat cream and detail-free: 46–91% across, 31–56% down; 7–93% across, 92–96% down; the box front at 15–31% across, 65–75% down. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, logos, labels, patterns or watermarks anywhere.

elements.text: Send it anyway. Delivered island-wide by Kapruka.

elements.brand: Kapruka (placed in Canva on the blank front face of the purple cake box, never painted by the image model)

why_it_works: Almost every Sri Lankan family has heard Amma say 'don't buy me anything'. The stacked title turns that line into a quote you read in one second.
The picture works without the headline: one hand says no while the other is already in the cake, with a slice gone and icing on her lip. The fork plays the part of the reference's pitchfork.

Figure and ground stay strict on flat cream. The only saturated masses are the purple box, the chocolate cake and the mother; the type is deep purple with two lighter-purple accents. The eye travels face → fork → box/logo → title → sign-off.
changes: Subject: the red stiletto melting into a pitchfork over a Biscoff jar becomes Amma, raised palm saying no and fork already in the cake. The melt/drip device is dropped because the concept doesn't need it; the fork stays as the plain, real-life version of the pitchfork.

Headline: 'THE / DEVIL / EATS / BISCOFF' becomes 'NO / GIFTS / SAID / AMMA'. The concept's two-line quote ('Don't buy me anything.' — Amma, every year) is 24 and 18 characters and can't fit the 3/5/4/7-character line limits, so it is shortened to the same meaning in 4 lines of 2/5/4/4 characters, all caps as in the reference.

Sign-off: 'Don't be silly Andrea, everybody wants this.' (44 chars) becomes the concept's supporting line 'Send it anyway. Delivered island-wide by Kapruka.' (49 chars, within the 50-char limit). It replaces 'A world of choices'; the two never run together.

Fonts: the Times-style film serif becomes Playfair Display 700, which keeps the high-contrast title rhythm the stacked lockup depends on (DM Serif Display has no 700). The tagline moves from rounded Nunito ExtraBold to Poppins Bold, the brand face.

Colours: the white ground becomes Soft Cream #F5F4EB, black type becomes Retail Purple #340A5C, and the red accent words and tagline become light purple #6B3FA0, which stays readable on a light ground. The red/caramel scene palette becomes Kapruka box purple #4B2386 with chocolate and skin tones.

Logo: the on-pack Biscoff label becomes ONE Kapruka logo in the same box, placed in Canva on the blank front of the purple cake box (on: dark). The image model paints the box plain and unprinted, and scene.attach is empty under the 2026-11-15 packaging rule.
Ornament removed: the arrow/devil-tail stroke through the V in DEVIL is dropped, since only flat blocks are allowed and the new word has no V.

Kept 'cutout-on-ground' framing as measured, so the concept's living-room setting is dropped: the mother and the cake box sit on the flat cream page with no room behind them. Her house dress keeps the at-home feel.
claims_used: 'Delivered island-wide' — 01-business-context.md §1 confirmed proof: 'Island-wide delivery — anywhere in Sri Lanka' (approved for ad use 2026-07-04).

'NO GIFTS SAID AMMA' — a quoted, relatable family line, not a factual claim. Cake as the gift is backed by §6 resolved item 7 (cakes are a top gifting category by revenue); the copy states no price, speed or offer.
